title: Spanning tree: root bridge and blocked port
summary: Break a switching loop with spanning tree and choose which switch becomes the root.
objectives: Turn spanning tree on in a looped topology
Choose the root bridge on purpose
Find out which port spanning tree blocks to remove the loop

tasks.title: Enable spanning tree
tasks.description: Three switches are cabled in a triangle, which is a layer 2 loop. Enable spanning tree on all three.
hints: Without spanning tree a broadcast would circle the triangle forever.
Spanning tree is a global setting: do it in system view on each switch.

criteria.label: Spanning tree is on for SW1
Spanning tree is on for SW2
Spanning tree is on for SW3

tasks.title: Make SW2 the root bridge
tasks.description: The switch with the lowest bridge priority becomes the root. Lower the priority of SW2 so it wins the election.
hints: Every switch starts with the same priority, so the lowest MAC address wins by default.
You only need to change SW2.
Example on SW2: stp root primary

tasks.title: Check that the loop is gone
tasks.description: With a root elected, spanning tree must block exactly one port in the triangle. It is on the link that does not touch the root.
hints: Look at the link between SW1 and SW3: both are one hop from the root, so one side has to give way.
If nothing is blocked, spanning tree is not enabled on every switch.
